orig.credit: Enoch Sontonga (first stanza, 1897) and S. E. K. Mqhayi (further stanzas, 1927); the historic Xhosa text as quoted in Wikipedia's article

stanzas: May its horn be raised up;
Come down, Spirit, come down, Spirit
May they fear him and revere him,
So that he may bless them.
Bless the men [?] of the nation,
Who carries the land with patience,
Of all the churches of this land;
Bless the farming and the livestock;
Drive out all famines and diseases;
Of coming together and of building ourselves up,
Of learning and of understanding one another
And its transgressions [?], and its sins

notes: line 1.2: 'upondo' is a horn; 'may its horn be raised' is the biblical image of strength and glory (as in the Psalms), not a musical horn.
line 2.1-2: 'Yihla' is 'come down, descend'; the stanza is a prayer to the Holy Spirit, as in Sontonga's hymn.

line 4.1: 'amadol'' read as 'amadolo', knees, used of those who hold the nation up (its elders or leaders); it could also be a misprint for 'amadoda', men. Unsure: please check against a printed Mqhayi text.

line 4.4, 5.4: 'Uwusikilele' carries an object concord (wu-) that does not match 'umlisela' or 'umtinjana' as nouns of class 1; translated loosely as 'it' / 'her'. Also note the spelling 'Uwusikilele' (4.4) beside 'Uwusikelele' (5.4) in the source.
line 5.1: 'amakosikazi' (modern amakhosikazi) can mean chiefs' wives, queens, or married women generally; rendered 'married women'.
line 6.2: 'imvaba' is a congregation or denomination; 'of all the churches' renders 'zonke iimvaba'.
line 8.2: 'ukuzaka' read as 'ukuzakha', to build oneself up (self-improvement); 'umanyano' is union, coming together.
line 8.4: the source has 'Uwasikele', apparently cut short for 'Uwasikelele'; translated as the other stanzas' last lines.
line 9.1: the source has 'Nkosi Sikelel, Afrika' with a stray comma; translated as stanza 1's first line.
line 9.3: 'Neziggito' looks like a misprint, probably for 'nezigqitho' (transgressions, trespasses); marked [?].
Spelling: the source keeps the older orthography (p for ph, t for th, k for kh: 'Malupakam'', 'umtinjana', 'amakosikazi'); left as it stands.
